sentences.text: Anticipatory Bail Application No. 1670 Of 2025

Rohan Ganesh Rathod
 Versus
 The State Of Maharashtra And Another
 ...

Advocate for Applicant : Mr. Aghav Abhishek Avinash a/w
 Mr. S.V. Jadhawar
 App for Respondent/State : Mr. P.D. Patil

Advocate for complainant : Mr. Kiran Rathod
 ...
 Coram : Mehroz K. Pathan, J.
 Date : 6th November 2025
Per Court :
1.

The Applicant has approached this Court, seeking
anticipatory bail in connection with Crime No.820/2023 registered
with Ambad Police Station, District Jalna for the offences punishable
under Sections 420, 406 read with 34 of the Indian Penal Code and
Sections 3, 4, 5 of the Mpid Act.
2.

It is the submission of the Counsel for the Applicant that the Applicant is apprehending his arrest in the aforesaid crime as though his name was not mentioned in the FIR, however after the investigation, it was found by the concerned Investigating Officer that one such entry in the accounts of the cooperative society, was showing an amount of transfer of Rs.9,00,000/- to the account of the present Applicant.
It is contention of the Applicant is that merely on  2 930.ABA-1670-2025.doc that ground, the application of the Applicant was rejected.
However there is no document to show that any such transaction had taken place.

He further relied upon one observation of the Special Judge,
Ambad in the case of Nitesh Pawar, wherein there is specific observation of the learned Sessions Judge that even though there was identical allegation of withdrawal of Rs.9,00,000/- from the account of the society against he arrested Nitesh Pawar, the prosecution had failed to show any documents to substantiate the same allegation.

sentences.text: The Applicant further submits that, being a respectable person and a director of the society, he would face disrepute if he is arrested.
He further submits that he is ready to cooperate with the investigation and would attend the police station.
His further submission is that since the other main accused persons are already released on bail, the custodial interrogation may not be necessary.
4. As against this, the learned APP submits that this is a serious economic offence wherein gullible investors are being lured by the Applicant and the multi-purpose co-operative society.

The Applicant,
being one of the directors, has played an important role in misappropriating the amount invested by the depositors.

5. Mr. Rathod, learned Counsel for the complainant, assisting the prosecution, has adopted the arguments of the learned APP and submits that the offence is serious in nature, and the Applicant may not be entitled to protection, as a thorough investigation is required.
The hard-earned money of many gullible investors has been siphoned off by the society, of which the Applicant is one of the directors.

6. After having gone through the investigation papers made available by the learned APP and orders granting regular bail to the main accused Sandesh Pawar and Nitesh Pawar by the learned Special Court The investigation papers do not show any document to substantiate the allegation of withdrawal of amount of Rs.9,00,000/-
by the present Applicant.

On the same ground, the learned Special Court has granted bail to the main accused that there is no such document in the investigation papers to substantiate the allegation of withdrawal of amount of Rs.9,00,000/- from the account of the society.
I am inclined to exercise the discretion under Section 438 of Cr.P.C.

Hence the following order :
 ORDER (i) In the event of arrest of the Applicant - Rohan Ganesh Rathod, be released on bail on furnishing P.R. bond of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousands) with one solvent surety in the like amount, in connection with Crime No.820/2023 registered with Ambad Police Station, District Jalna, on the following conditions :
(a) The Applicant is directed to attend the concerned police station and report to the Investigating Officer between 11:00 a.m. to 01:00 p.m. on every Monday, and as and when called by the Investigating Officer.

(c) The Applicant shall not pressurize the prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence, in any manner.

8. Stand over to 27.11.2025.
